items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The musicians I knew were Jimmy Hamilton, Sonny Greer, Harry Carney, Ray Nance, Al Killian, Russel Procope, Quinton Jackson, Johnny Hodges, the Duke himself...

ctx.x: I had a room in a place called Pensione Beccari on the via del Tritone and to cut down on expenses, I shared a two roomed bedroom with a hungarian fellow named Pista. Pista was a refugee, and there were quite a number of them-men and women-staying in this pensione. But the day that Lily returned, I moved to another room in the same place. While at this place, I met a West Indian fellow named Stanley Carter. I had heard of him, but never seen him. Stanley played piano and sang. His act was on the style of Morris…

Duke Ellington was on his first tour of Europe after world war II and it was a delightful pleasure to know that he would be coming to Rome during the time I was there. This was in May and Duke played a theatre for 5 to 6 concerts. It was something for Lily also, because she had never seen or heard of a big band playing jazz. The musicians I knew were Jimmy Hamilton, Sonny Greer, Harry Carney, Ray Nance, Al Killian, Russel Procope, Quinton Jackson, Johnny Hodges, the Duke himself, Don Byas who had been engaged to…

The new musicians that I did not know but had the opportunity to meet were Ernie Royal, a trumpetist, Alvin McCain, a tenor man, Butch Ballard a drummer that Duke had engaged to play the serious drum parts while Sonny featured on certain numbers that called for his showmanship. I didn't know Wendell Marshall, the bass player, but Lily and I went to four concerts and eventually we became acquainted with all the musicians I had not known before and that was the first time that I had heard Duke and his men so many…
